us-midterms.summary: In the U.S. elections, Democrats scored a notable success and are now, according to AP, France 24 and other outlets, increasing pressure on Donald Trump and his agenda. Democrats say their priorities include investigating alleged corruption, overseeing ICE, and tackling the rising cost of living. Los Angeles? ai-market-selloff.title: Global markets are rattled by a fresh selloff in AI stocks and fears of overheating data centers
ai-market-selloff.summary: Global markets are selling off stocks tied to artificial intelligence amid new fears that the sector is overheating. FT says the trigger was investors’ reaction to the U.S. election results, while other reports point to growing unease around data centers and demand for AI infrastructure. France 24 notes that Democrats in the U.S. and regulators in Europe want stricter oversight of data centers, and separate articles highlight disputes over the energy and environmental cost of this boom. europe-protests.title: Europe is hit by a wave of false bomb threats, disrupting flights and broadcasts
europe-protests.summary: Europe is facing a continuing series of false bomb threats that have disrupted flights and forced newsrooms to evacuate. AP, Reuters, France 24 and other outlets report that the threats have affected airlines and European media organizations, while Irish authorities say this is part of a coordinated destabilization campaign. At the same time, France is preparing for fresh mass protests: unions, students and the Yellow Vest movement are calling for “mass civil disobedience,” and authorities are deploying tens of thousands of officers. The result is a European backdrop shaped by both security threats and social unrest.

pope-south-america-tour.title: Pope Leo begins a South America tour soon after surgery and speaks about health and access to care
pope-south-america-tour.summary: Pope Leo XIV began a trip through South America soon after surgery on his lungs. According to AP, BBC and France 24, the first stop was Uruguay, and the pontiff said he feels better than he looks and is in fairly good condition. On his first trip he also called for universal access to healthcare; one report adds that in Uruguay he said AI development should expand people’s opportunities rather than make workers “expendable.” The trip is scheduled to last 12 days and include several countries in the region.

iran-us-friction.title: The U.S. and Iran are balancing on the edge of a new escalation with Qatar’s mediation
iran-us-friction.summary: The U.S. and Iran remain on the brink of a new escalation, while Qatar is trying to act as a mediator. Reuters, CBS, AP and other outlets report that Washington is offering $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear program, while Qatar is urging both sides not to wait for the “best moment” to settle the dispute. Against this backdrop, there are reports of new strikes and a sharp exchange of statements: Trump is sending mixed signals about a possible attack, while Iran says its forces are stronger than at the start of the war. Some reports also link the tension to the fact that the U.S. president is sending contradictory signals after the midterm defeat.

paraguay-bank-collapse.title: In Paraguay, a new power arrangement begins after the impeachment and arrest of the former president
paraguay-bank-collapse.summary: In Paraguay, the banking crisis led to the impeachment of President Santiago Peña, his arrest, and the transfer of power to the vice president. AP, BBC, Reuters, The Guardian and Le Monde write that after the bank collapse, millions of customers lost access to their accounts and savings, triggering a political collapse. According to different reports, Peña was first removed by parliament and then placed under house arrest; the new head of state, Pedro Aliana, has already been sworn in. The outlets agree that the financial scandal exposed the close ties between politics and finance in the country.

ukraine-oleshky.summary: Russia launched massive strikes on Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine, damaging energy facilities and causing outages in electricity, water and heating. TASS, DW, France 24, Reuters and Ukrainian media report destruction in Kyiv and the Kyiv region; according to various accounts, there are dead and injured, including a man pulled from the rubble. Volodymyr Zelensky said the supply situation in the capital is difficult and that Moscow is trying to plunge Ukraine into a blackout, in his words. The response also includes reported Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure and talks involving the U.S. and Russia.

kenya-cult-sentencing.title: In Kenya, sect leader sentenced to 200 years over the deaths of hundreds of children
kenya-cult-sentencing.summary: In Kenya, sect leader Paul Mackenzie was sentenced to 200 years in prison for the deaths of 190 children and one adult. Reuters, AP, NYT and other outlets report that he told his followers to starve themselves so they could “meet Jesus,” which led to the mass death of people. The court found him guilty of murder and imposed a lengthy sentence. Some reports note that public reaction to the ruling was mixed: some people considered the sentence fair, while others said it was not enough.

israel-election.title: In Israel, the deadlock over forming a coalition continues after the election
israel-election.summary: In Israel, a deadlock over forming a government remains after the election. AP, NYT, Al Jazeera and other outlets write that President Isaac Herzog must task one of the candidates with trying to assemble a coalition after the inconclusive vote. At the center of the discussion are blocs around Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot and the Arab parties; according to several reports, support from Arab lists could prove decisive. france-protests.summary: France is once again preparing for mass protests and strikes over the rising cost of living. The interior ministry, according to the reports, is preparing to mobilize 70,000 police and security forces. British and international agencies note that the protests are taking place amid anger over people’s purchasing power.

russia-state-pressure-assets.summary: Reports in Russian and Russia-related outlets point to growing state control over business, assets and internal discipline. Separate reports also concern Belarus: Lukashenko said he does not support revolution and does not want a repeat of such events. Reuters, AP, The Guardian and News24 write that the party is on about 32 percent and is losing control of key municipalities, including Mangaung. The opposition DA is strengthening its position, while new players are emerging in some cities and could become kingmakers in coalition talks. Reuters and SCMP report that, according to Swiss group IQAir, the Indian capital ranked first for air pollution on Saturday morning. diwali-festival-lights.summary: Diwali is being celebrated around the world as the festival of lights. giant-banner-targets-big-tech.summary: In Switzerland, Greenpeace activists hung a giant anti-Big Tech banner near a data center construction site. Euronews reports that the action took place in Beringen in the northeast of the country and was aimed at the growing environmental impact of major technology companies. The outlet describes it as a protest against the data center project and, more broadly, against high-energy digital infrastructure. It is a local action, but one that fits into the wider European debate over data centers.
